sn48.1:1.3: _Indriya_ (“faculty”) is an abstract noun from _indra_, the name of the potent Vedic god of war. In the Vedas, Indra manifests his _indriya_ by drinking soma. The drug enables him to release his full potential and power; originally this probably referred to drinking an amphetamine-like substance before battle. Thus _indriya_ means “faculty” in the sense “capability”, but also has the sense “potential, potency”.
sn48.1:1.4: This Saṁyutta is unique in that it gathers several different kinds of things under the banner of _indriya_: the five spiritual faculties predominate; the sense faculties, usually reckoned as six ([sn48.25]()–30), but only five in [sn48.41]() and [sn48.42](); the five faculties of feeling ([sn48.31]()–40); the three faculties pertaining to life ([sn48.22]()); the three faculties pertaining to enlightenment ([sn48.23](). Together these were systematized as the Abhidhamma set of 22 faculties ([vb5]()).
sn48.1:1.5: These are the five so-called “spiritual faculties”, whose specification is identical to the “five powers” ([sn50.1-12]()). For definitions, see [sn48.8](), [sn48.9](), and [sn48.10]().
